subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics Advanced, Year 11
about: HSC, Functions, trigonometry, calculus and probability
syllabus: NSW Mathematics Advanced 11-12 Syllabus (2024), Year 11 focus areas

points.title: Functions and relations
points.brief: A relation pairs inputs with outputs. A function gives exactly one output for each input. On a graph, the vertical line test tells them apart.

points.title: Domain and range
points.brief: The domain is the set of allowed x values and the range is the set of y values produced. Students find both, including for square roots and fractions.

points.title: Function notation
points.brief: Writing f(x) and evaluating it, such as f(3) or f(a + 1), and using it to describe a rule.

points.title: Odd and even functions
points.brief: An even function has f(-x) = f(x) and is symmetric in the y-axis. An odd function has f(-x) = -f(x) and has point symmetry about the origin.

points.title: Linear functions
points.brief: Gradient as rise over run, the forms y = mx + c and y - y₁ = m(x - x₁), parallel lines with equal gradients and perpendicular lines whose gradients multiply to -1.

points.title: Quadratic functions
points.brief: Parabolas, their axis of symmetry x = -b/2a, vertex, intercepts and whether they open up or down. Finding roots by factorising, completing the square and the quadratic formula.

points.title: The discriminant
points.brief: Δ = b² - 4ac tells how many real roots a quadratic has, two if positive, one if zero, none if negative. It also decides whether a line meets a parabola.

points.title: Cubic and polynomial graphs
points.brief: Sketching cubics from their factors, using roots, the y-intercept and what happens as x grows large. A repeated root touches the axis.

points.title: Reciprocal functions
points.brief: The hyperbola y = k/x, with asymptotes on both axes, and how the sign of k decides which quadrants it lies in.

points.title: Absolute value functions
points.brief: |x| is the distance from zero. The graph of y = |x| is a V shape, and solving |x - a| = b gives two answers.

points.title: Circles
points.brief: The circle (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² has centre (h, k) and radius r. Completing the square turns a general equation into this form.

points.title: Vertical translations
points.brief: y = f(x) + c moves the graph up by c, or down if c is negative.

points.title: Horizontal translations
points.brief: y = f(x + b) moves the graph left by b. The shift is the opposite of the sign, a common mistake.

points.title: Vertical dilations
points.brief: y = kf(x) stretches the graph from the x-axis by a factor of k. Every y value is multiplied by k.

points.title: Horizontal dilations
points.brief: y = f(ax) compresses the graph towards the y-axis by a factor of a, so every x value is divided by a.

points.title: Reflections
points.brief: y = -f(x) reflects in the x-axis and y = f(-x) reflects in the y-axis.

points.title: Solving equations with graphs
points.brief: The solutions of f(x) = g(x) are the x values where the two graphs meet. Counting intersections tells how many solutions there are.

points.title: Right-angled trigonometry
points.brief: Sine, cosine and tangent as ratios of sides in a right-angled triangle, used to find unknown sides and angles.

points.title: Exact values
points.brief: The exact trig ratios of 30°, 45° and 60° from the two special triangles, written with surds.

points.title: Bearings and elevation
points.brief: True bearings measured clockwise from north as three digits, and angles of elevation and depression, applied in two-step problems.

points.title: Radians
points.brief: One radian is the angle where the arc equals the radius. π radians is 180°, and students convert between the two.

points.title: Arcs and sectors
points.brief: Arc length l = rθ and sector area A = ½r²θ, with θ in radians.

points.title: The sine rule
points.brief: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C for any triangle. The ambiguous case, where two triangles fit the given side and angle.

points.title: The cosine rule
points.brief: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C, used when two sides and the included angle, or all three sides, are known.

points.title: Area of any triangle
points.brief: Area = ½ab sin C, using two sides and the angle between them.

points.title: The unit circle
points.brief: On a circle of radius 1, cos θ is the x-coordinate and sin θ the y-coordinate. The signs in each quadrant follow from this.

points.title: Angles of any size
points.brief: Using related acute angles and the quadrant to find trig ratios of angles beyond 90°, in degrees and radians.

points.title: Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent
points.brief: The shapes, periods and amplitudes of y = sin x, y = cos x and y = tan x, and where tan has asymptotes.

points.title: Reciprocal ratios
points.brief: Cosecant, secant and cotangent as 1/sin, 1/cos and 1/tan, and where each is undefined.

points.title: The Pythagorean identity
points.brief: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and the related identities with tan and sec, used to simplify expressions and prove identities.

points.title: Solving trigonometric equations
points.brief: Finding every solution of an equation such as 2 sin x = 1 within a given domain, using the quadrants and the period.

chapters.title: Rates of change and the derivative

points.title: Average rate of change
points.brief: The gradient of a secant between two points on a curve, (f(b) - f(a))/(b - a), as an average rate of change.

points.title: The derivative from first principles
points.brief: The derivative is the limit of the secant gradient as h approaches 0, f'(x) = lim (f(x + h) - f(x))/h. It gives the gradient of the tangent.

points.title: The power rule
points.brief: The derivative of xⁿ is nxⁿ⁻¹, including negative and fractional powers, and the derivatives of sums and constant multiples.

points.title: Tangents and normals
points.brief: Using the derivative at a point to find the equation of the tangent, and the normal, which is perpendicular to it.

points.title: Where a function is not differentiable
points.brief: A function has no derivative at a sharp corner, a jump or a vertical tangent, even if it is continuous there.

points.title: The product rule
points.brief: The derivative of uv is u'v + uv'.

points.title: The quotient rule
points.brief: The derivative of u/v is (u'v - uv')/v². A common mistake is the order of the terms on top.

points.title: The chain rule
points.brief: The derivative of f(g(x)) is f'(g(x)) × g'(x), as in differentiating (3x + 1)⁵.

points.title: Derivatives as rates in context
points.brief: Interpreting a derivative as a rate, such as velocity as the rate of change of displacement, with units.

points.title: Exponential functions
points.brief: Graphs of y = aˣ for a > 1 and 0 < a < 1, their horizontal asymptote and y-intercept of 1.

points.title: The number e
points.brief: e is about 2.718. y = eˣ is the exponential whose gradient at every point equals its value, so the derivative of eˣ is eˣ.

points.title: What a logarithm is
points.brief: log_a(x) is the power a must be raised to, to give x. So log₂ 8 = 3. Logarithms undo exponentials.

points.title: Logarithm laws
points.brief: log(xy) = log x + log y, log(x/y) = log x - log y, and log(xⁿ) = n log x, plus log_a(1) = 0 and log_a(a) = 1.

points.title: Change of base
points.brief: log_a(x) = log_b(x)/log_b(a), which lets a calculator find a logarithm in any base.

points.title: Solving exponential equations
points.brief: Taking logarithms of both sides to solve equations such as 3ˣ = 20, and using the natural log ln for base e.

points.title: Graphs of logarithmic functions
points.brief: y = log_a(x) is the reflection of y = aˣ in the line y = x. It has a vertical asymptote at x = 0 and passes through (1, 0).

points.title: Sample spaces and probability
points.brief: Listing all equally likely outcomes, and P(event) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes, between 0 and 1.

points.title: Venn diagrams and set notation
points.brief: Union, intersection and complement, shown on Venn diagrams, and P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B).

points.title: Conditional probability
points.brief: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B), the probability of A given that B has happened, read from tables and diagrams.

points.title: Independent events
points.brief: Events are independent when one does not change the probability of the other, so P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

points.title: Multi-stage experiments
points.brief: Tree diagrams and arrays for two or more stages, with and without replacement.

points.title: Types of data
points.brief: Categorical data (nominal or ordinal) and numerical data (discrete or continuous), and which displays suit each.

points.title: Measures of centre
points.brief: The mean, median and mode, and why the median is better than the mean when data has outliers or is skewed.

points.title: Measures of spread
points.brief: Range, interquartile range and standard deviation, and what each says about how spread out data is.

points.title: Shape of a distribution
points.brief: Describing data as symmetric or positively or negatively skewed, and spotting outliers with the 1.5 × IQR rule.
